design.md:197-206 '## Security Boundaries' names B1-B4 and explicitly defers authoritative treatment to security-spec.md (design.md:199: 'The authoritative treatment is security-spec.md ... which is a normative layer of this specification'). requirements.md:296-318 and design.md:349-378 record that OQ-1 (the consent-scope unit, which is the authentication/authorization mechanism at boundaries B1 and B4) was resolved by the human on 2026-08-04 as 'feature and session; both must match.' security-spec.md was not updated to match: it still contains the literal unresolved placeholder text describing the auth mechanism at boundary B1 (security-spec.md:81, table cell 'human consent, once per OQ-1 scope') and at B4 in the trust-boundary diagram (security-spec.md:71, 'per OQ-1 scope'), and the 'Under Whose Consent' table (security-spec.md:45, 'once per OQ-1 scope'). security-spec.md's own '## Open Questions' section (183-189) still lists OQ-1 through OQ-5 as open, with OQ-1/OQ-2 marked as blocking REQ-001/REQ-004, with no acknowledgment anywhere in the file of the 2026-08-04 resolutions documented in requirements.md and design.md. A reader consulting the document design.md names as authoritative for these boundaries would find an unresolved auth-mechanism placeholder and a blocking open question that both requirements.md and design.md say was closed -- an internal contradiction in the normative security refinement on exactly the item this check requires ('the authentication/authorization mechanism at each boundary'). Major: a downstream implementer or later reviewer consulting security-spec.md as ground truth would be misled into treating the scope rule as still undecided.
